title: Last Car in the Garage
story: A small parking garage logs a car's ticket number twice: once when it drives in, once when it drives out. The log is one long list in no useful order.
At closing time exactly one car is still inside, so exactly one ticket appears only once. The gate computer can read the log once but has almost no spare memory.
task: Write carStillInside(log). Every ticket number in log appears exactly twice, except one that appears exactly once. Return that number.
Aim for one pass and O(1) extra memory: no map, no set, no sorted copy.
constraints: Exactly one number appears once. Every other number appears exactly twice.

examples.explanation: 512 came in and went out. So did 87. 340 appears once, so that car is still inside.
The two 4s are neighbours, but the two 9s are not. Do not assume partners sit together. The answer is 2.

hints: What is x XOR x for any number x? And x XOR 0?
XOR of a number with itself is 0, and XOR with 0 changes nothing. XOR also ignores order: a ^ b ^ a equals a ^ a ^ b.
So what if you XOR every ticket in the log together? Each pair cancels, wherever its halves sit. What is left?
Start with result = 0 and XOR in every number. The pairs cancel, leaving the one ticket with no partner.
bruteForce: Counting tickets in a hash map is O(n) time but stores up to n / 2 numbers, which the gate computer cannot afford. Checking each ticket against every other uses no memory but costs O(n²): about 900 million comparisons for 30,001 entries.
Sorting, then comparing neighbours in steps of two, uses little memory but costs O(n log n) and needs a sortable copy or permission to reorder the log.

js: * @param {number[]} log  every ticket twice except one

tests.note: the answer is 0 and sits at the start
the answer is at the very end
pairs are not next to each other
1 ^ 2 = 3: summing or OR-ing the distinct values would be wrong
the lone ticket is 0, in the middle: a "found yet?" check on the value 0 breaks

js: result ^= ticket; // pairs cancel: x ^ x = 0
py: result ^= ticket  # pairs cancel: x ^ x = 0
walkthrough: XOR compares two numbers bit by bit and gives 1 where the bits differ. Two facts do the work: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x. Order does not matter, so every pair cancels however far apart its halves are.
The middle values (13, 11) look like nonsense. Only the final value matters.
solution.takeaway: XOR is a cancel button: anything appearing an even number of times vanishes. Use it to find the odd one out among pairs, or a difference without extra memory.
